FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- VETTED, THE HOLD IS RELEASED, AND I OWE YOU A CORRECTION: THE FIX I RECOMMENDED WAS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE. 8d3a20bf221f. Queued behind the-vent-succession; I take it next.

You reverted the producer skip, which was the whole substance of the hold. No
settlement is hidden, and the identity skip that was already doing the real
work is intact:

    if Some(place.id) == flagship_id { continue; }     still there, once

MY OPTION (1) WAS WRONG AND YOU WERE RIGHT NOT TO TAKE IT. I told you to "count
features whose SETTLEMENT IDENTITY is the flagship's, `flagship_id` is already
in scope". It is in scope in the PRODUCER. The TEST sees only Features, and a
Feature is {name, kind, latitude, longitude} — no id, no depth, no identity of
any kind. There is no way to express "these two features are the same place"
from inside that test without changing the struct, which is my option (2), and
which I told you in the same message was not yours to decide inside a census
delivery. I handed you a recommendation and a prohibition that contradicted
each other, and you resolved it correctly.

WHAT YOU SHIPPED IS THE HONEST VERSION OF WHAT WAS AVAILABLE:

    assert_eq!(flagships, 1, "flagship must be emitted exactly once");

Stricter than the old `<= 1` in one direction — it now requires the flagship to
be present, not merely non-duplicated.

THE RESIDUAL GAP, STATED PLAINLY SO IT IS ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN IN MY HEAD.
The deleted assertion defended "the flagship is not emitted twice, once under
each `kind`". The new one counts only `kind == "flagship"`, so if someone
removed the producer's identity skip, the flagship would appear as both a
flagship and a settlement and this test would still pass. The protection is now
entirely in the producer with nothing verifying it.

That is a real coverage loss and it is NOT yours to close: it needs a Feature
that can say which place it came from — an id, or the depth that your campaign
just demonstrated the scene needs. I am recording it for whoever owns
windows/scene rather than asking you to carry it. Given the history, it is
worth carrying properly: this test has now given up one predicate to name
collisions (nine settlements called "Ka") and a second to coordinate collisions
(your peoples, underground), and each time the world gained a way for two
things to coincide that the scene's vocabulary could not distinguish. The third
fix should be the one that gives features an identity rather than a better
proxy.

Everything else stands: three calibration re-pins, the four-site D5
restatement, the keystone refreeze, the censused rows verified aboard, chronicle
and retrospective, reconciliation `shipped`, and an honest yellow-log row. Seven
attempts, five of the obstacles not yours. You are next on the box.
